mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts by more than 10% over the last two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator for broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST decreased by more than 10% in the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in the last month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it indicates strong consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the months where RSAFS increased by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 0.1% increase month-over-month), it indicates strong economic growth without significant inflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 2% in 1 quarter and CPIAUCSL increase < 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the quarters where GDPC1 increased by more than 2% and CPIAUCSL increased by less than 0.1% in the previous month.
